Though this term to an extent carries the meaning you have in mind, there is a more helpful description. You are conflating two issues into one:

  • Left - Right (State vs Individual) The Fiscal Dimension
  • Authoritarian - Libertarian (More or less power to the Government) The Social Dimension

Instead of viewing people and politicians along a single axis, look at them along both these axes.

For example, both Stalin and Hitler were about equally Authoritarian, but they differed in how Left or RIght they were, how much they thought the state should own/control.

The group you had in mind would be better described as Stalinist, than Fascist.

There is clear information about this at Political Compass

I try my best to avoid typical left-right words when describing the political leanings of groups or individuals. That is because it is very seldom for a group or person to be completely left or completely right. For example the Nordic Resistance Movement, a National Socialist group, is described in media as far right-extremists. But in actuality, the majority of their policies are very left. But their immigration policy is very right. And some of their leftist policies have caveats and exceptions that make them both left and right. See how confusing, useless and possibly misleading the left-right thing is?

See how confusing, useless and possibly misleading the left-right thing is?

It is not that confusing, really. Where people go wrong is by trying to combine two entirely different factors into one.

Here is an analogy which might help explain things. One scale is distance (Near or Far). People can talk about something being very near or further away and there is no confusion. What about when you wish to include an additional factor, such as altitude (High or Low)? It is possible (just about) to continue to use only the distance scale to describe both the height and range of something, but you are losing information if you do so. It is much better to make reference to two scales, which would give you this:

  • Near and High
  • Near and Low
  • Far and High
  • Far and Low

The mass media very seldom makes use of this "second axis", the one that indicates how Authoritarian a political candidate is. Perhaps they think it might 'confuse' people, though I think it might unconfuse them!
